The page's copy button gives you this text. Paste it into Gemini, then paste your notes under it. The Gemini skill in `skill/ppt-outline/` carries the same text.

Turn the notes I give you into a slide outline for a presentation in a Hong Kong office. The audience is colleagues or managers watching the slides on a projector. A tool will read the outline and fill it into the company's PowerPoint template, so the format below must be exact.
Output only the outline, inside one code block, in this format:
Subtitle line: team, date or occasion, only if the notes give one
- Start with one # line for the title slide. Every other slide starts with ##.
- At most 6 points per slide. At most 30 characters per point; a Chinese character counts as one.
- Use || only when the slide compares two things side by side, such as two options or before and after.
- A ## line with nothing under it makes a section divider slide.
- Keep every number, date, amount and name exactly as the notes write it. Add no fact, number or example that is not in the notes. If the notes do not say something, leave it out.
- Write in the language of the notes. For Chinese notes, write Traditional Chinese as used in Hong Kong business documents: written Chinese, not spoken Cantonese.
- No bold, no italics, no emoji, and no text before or after the code block.
# 用公司 PPT 範本出簡報
將你嘅筆記變成一份用公司範本做嘅 PowerPoint。每個標題、每一點都放入範本本身嘅格仔，公司 logo、顏色、字體原封不動，下載之後照樣可以改。
1. 喺網頁撳「複製」，貼落 Gemini，再貼埋你嘅筆記。Gemini 會俾你一段大綱。
2. 將公司範本（`.pptx` 或 `.potx`）拖入網頁。
範本同簡報全程留喺你部電腦：網頁載入完之後唔會再連網，熄咗 Wi-Fi 都用得。大綱嗰一步會將筆記交俾 Gemini；唔想交嘅話，可以跟網頁個例子自己打大綱。
適合個人 Gemini 帳戶。
2. 去 gemini.google.com，左邊揀 Customize，再揀 Skills，撳 Create，揀 Upload，揀呢個檔案。
3. 之後喺 Gemini 打 `/`，揀 ppt-outline，再貼筆記。

Turn the notes I give you into a slide outline for a presentation in a Hong Kong office. The audience is colleagues or managers watching the slides on a projector. A tool will read the outline and fill it into the company's PowerPoint template, so the format below must be exact.
Output only the outline, inside one code block, in this format:
Subtitle line: team, date or occasion, only if the notes give one
- Start with one # line for the title slide. Every other slide starts with ##.
- At most 6 points per slide. At most 30 characters per point; a Chinese character counts as one.
- Use || only when the slide compares two things side by side, such as two options or before and after.
- A ## line with nothing under it makes a section divider slide.
- Keep every number, date, amount and name exactly as the notes write it. Add no fact, number or example that is not in the notes. If the notes do not say something, leave it out.
- Write in the language of the notes. For Chinese notes, write Traditional Chinese as used in Hong Kong business documents: written Chinese, not spoken Cantonese.
- No bold, no italics, no emoji, and no text before or after the code block.

A static page in `docs/` loads Pyodide, python-pptx and `deckfill` from its own origin, then locks the network by adding a second Content Security Policy (`connect-src 'none'; img-src data: blob:; worker-src 'none'`). The user's template, outline and deck stay in the tab: `deckfill.web.Session` reads, plans and fills on the main thread, and the deck leaves as a `blob:` download.
The parts the diff does not spell out:

- `fill` re-zips every output and puts the template's own bytes back for every kept part whose meaning is unchanged (`src/deckfill/fill.py`, `_restore_kept`). It also writes each slide's own number into copied slide-number fields.
- The page reaches Python through a hook on `window` only when the URL hash is `#e2e` (`docs/app.js`, in `loadEngine`).
## The one fact it is safe because of
After ready, the page makes no request of any kind. Proven at step 4 (ran real code) on HEAD `fc505ff`.

`node tests/e2e/c9_privacy.mjs` drives the real page in headless Chromium and saves every browser request and every server hit with times (`qa/e2e/c9-report.json`). The session covers open, ready, two fills with downloads (one with a layout override), reset, 30 s idle, an offline fill and a click on each link-out. `qa/e2e/privacy_proof.py` reads that saved log:
session 33 s; 20 browser requests, 19 server hits
before ready: 19 requests, 0 to another origin
after ready: 1 browser requests, of which 1 are clicked link-outs (https://mentron.hk/)
after ready: 0 page requests, 0 server hits, 0 blocked attempts
fills after ready: 2 with downloads, plus one offline
PASS: zero page requests after ready

It also fails when it should. The two C9 mutations (a same-origin fetch one second after each download, and outline text in the Gemini link) both fail the session (`qa/failure-demos/c9-*-mutated.txt`). After ready, `fetch` from page JS and from Python (`js.fetch`, `pyodide.http.pyfetch`), same origin and other origin, and new workers (URL, `blob:`, `data:`) are all blocked by the browser.

- **Memory at the input caps.** Spec rev 5 set a bar: wasm heap 1.5 GB or less at the D1b worst case. At the rev 5 caps (100 MB file, 150 MB uncompressed) the worst case reached 1,674 MB, so the seat lowered the uncompressed cap to 130 MB. There it reaches 1,384 MB (99.5 MiB file, 129.5 MiB uncompressed); at the old rev 4 caps it reached 2.39 GB. Wasm memory never shrinks, so a long session with many large templates stays at its high point. HKUST template 14 (73.7 MB) fills within the bars. Check: `node tests/e2e/c12_load.mjs` (bar `worstHeapMB`). Evidence: `qa/e2e/c12-report.json`, `decisions.tsv`.

- **GitHub Pages MIME types and headers.** Not proven locally. The page needs `application/wasm` for `pyodide.asm.wasm` and a JavaScript type for `.mjs`. Check at the deploy gate: Fable's real-Chrome run on the Pages URL (root Rule 127). Likelihood low (Pages serves both types), cost high (page never reaches ready, so it fails closed, with no leak).

- **Warm load sits on its bar.** The second visit took 5.0 s against 5 s, because the headless test profile's memory cache does not keep the 9.6 MB wasm. A real Chrome profile has a disk cache. Check in real Chrome at the deploy gate.

- **Subpath.** Pages serves the site at `/ppt-template/`. A scratch server mounted `docs/` there: ready, fill and download all worked, 19 requests all inside `/ppt-template/`, 0 after ready. Every page URL is relative (`new URL("./", location.href)` in `docs/app.js`; `fonts/...` in `docs/style.css`).

- **Pyodide's default CDN.** `pyodide.mjs` falls back to jsdelivr when `packageBaseUrl` is unset. `app.js` sets it to the vendor folder, and the static origin check allowlists only that string, with the reason.

- **Lazy loads after ready.** All Python modules are imported before the lockdown. A missing module would raise, not fetch. The 2 fills plus 1 offline fill after ready made 0 requests. Each font family is one file, loaded through `document.fonts.load` before ready. User text outside the Noto Serif TC subset falls back to a system font, with no request.

- **`_restore_kept` restoring a part the fill meant to change.** Every intended change is excluded by name (the presentation part and its `.rels`, `[Content_Types].xml`, `docProps/app.xml`) or by content type (slide and notes parts). Otherwise it differs in meaning (a layout `.rels` or XML with a hyperlink to a removed slide), so it is not restored. C3 on `sections` checks the hyperlink removal survives. 173 tests pass. The isolated mutation demo is `qa/failure-demos/c3-rels-order-*.txt`.
- **The `#e2e` hook.** It exposes the page's own Pyodide to the page's own window. It adds no request (the hash never reaches a server) and no new reader of the user's data.

- **Download names.** `file_name` strips Windows-unsafe characters and collapses spaces (`tests/test_web_bridge.py`). Windows reserved device names (`CON`) are left to Chrome's own download-name rules. Unproven, low cost: the user renames the file.
- **Other browsers.** The spec targets Chrome and Edge on Windows. Firefox and Safari behaviour of a CSP meta added after load was not tested.
- `node tests/e2e/c9_privacy.mjs && .venv/bin/python qa/e2e/privacy_proof.py` on the commit that ships.
- `node tests/e2e/c12_load.mjs` for the memory and timing numbers.
- At deploy: the Pages URL in real Chrome, ready and one fill, with DevTools Network open after ready.

Walkthrough artifact is available at f6c30a9:qa/walkthrough/walkthrough.json:1, but absent at 884f33a; its claims were checked against 884f33a. Known cap/heap changes and missing .NET execution excluded. No files changed. Targeted probes ran pinned code in memory; full browser suite was not rerun.

Download can silently omit latest edits. Input schedules replanning 450 ms later while previous plan remains downloadable. Download calls Session.fill() against cached plan (f6c30a9:src/deckfill/web.py:80-81). Pinned-JS probe changed textarea to NEW CONTENT and immediately downloaded OLD CONTENT. Fix: invalidate download synchronously on input and await planning of current outline and overrides before filling. Likelihood: ordinary edit or paste followed by immediate download.

XML security checks depend on filename extension. A slide-layout XML part renamed to .dat, with relationships and content type updated, bypasses XML-specific caps and DOCTYPE rejection. Pinned-engine probes accepted both an oversized XML layout and a DOCTYPE containing an entity declaration. No entity expansion or disclosure observed. Fix: identify XML through OPC content types as well as relationship filenames, then enforce byte limits and safe parsing before python-pptx opens it. Likelihood: crafted malicious template; uncommon accidental input.

Member limit runs after central-directory allocation. ZipFile constructs every ZipInfo before code checks the 2,000-member cap. A 47,000,053-byte crafted archive containing 1,000,000 central-directory records eventually raised too_big, but CPython process peak RSS reached 510.4 MiB, versus 162.6 MiB before parsing. This is separate from excluded accepted-input heap changes. Fix: bounded central-directory preflight before ZipFile construction, including actual record count and ZIP64/count inconsistencies. Likelihood: adversarial archive; browser memory impact was not measured.

Long-word wrapping can monopolize main thread. Width is subtracted repeatedly from token width; a tiny positive usable box width remains accepted (f6c30a9:src/deckfill/template.py:266-272). With normal 20-point text and 1 EMU usable width, 50 characters required about 7 million iterations. A near-limit outline implies billions; full browser duration was not measured. Fix: calculate line count and remainder with constant-time arithmetic, and test tiny widths. Likelihood: adversarial or damaged placeholder geometry.

Integrity check misses package-root relationships. It skips _rels/.rels and never validates all relationships from source "". Probe added a root relationship targeting missing.xml; check_integrity returned no problems and read_template accepted it. Fix: validate root targets and external URIs alongside part relationships. Spec L149: "every internal relationship target resolves to a part in the package". Likelihood: damaged or crafted template.

Removing sample slides can make otherwise accepted templates unfillable. Generic XML parts, including viewProps.xml, lack _element. Code removes their slide relationships but leaves XML references intact. A saved outline-view reference passed input integrity, then fill raised "bad_file: output failed integrity: id=rId1 names no relationship in ppt/viewProps.xml". Fix: safely parse and update generic XML blobs when removing references. Spec L150: "Any element in a kept part whose relationship points to a removed slide ... is removed together with that relationship." Likelihood: uncommon saved outline-view state. Synthetic case was not SDK-validated.

Subtitle-to-body fallback bypasses fit checks. Title slides receive unconditional fits even when subtitle targets a content body. A 4,000-character subtitle overridden onto a content layout produced one slide, fits, and no warning. Fix: estimate subtitle paragraphs when their destination is a body and return warned/check status as appropriate. Spec L165: "For each body, plan_deck estimates the text height". Likelihood: supported fallback or override with long subtitle.

Positioned slide-local footers disappear. Code finds an example footer, then discards it if destination layout lacks that footer placeholder, even when source footer has explicit geometry. Pinned-engine probe lost LOCAL FOOTER text without warning. Fix: preserve positioned source footer and resolve geometry where needed. Spec L155: "Input slides on the same layout: if one carries the type, the new slide gets it, copied from the first such slide". Likelihood: uncommon customized corporate template.

Prompt-load failure leaves an apparently ready page copying empty text. Boot swallows fetch rejection and loads engine anyway; copy closure remains empty. Retry updates displayed prompt but never updates that closure. HTTP errors are also not checked (f6c30a9:docs/app.js:126-129). Fix: disable copying until prompt loads successfully, surface failures, check response status, and use same setter on retry. Likelihood: intermittent initial resource failure.

C9 PASS lacks required session coverage. Saved ready-to-link interval is only 5.247 seconds (f6c30a9:qa/e2e/c9-report.json:143-164), contradicting claimed 30-second idle coverage. Mutation runner sets IDLE_MS=3000 and overwrites same report (f6c30a9:qa/failure-demos/run_demos.py:74-78). Only Mentron link was recorded; test swallows click failures and requires merely one link-out. Fix: separate mutation evidence, assert elapsed idle duration, preserve page while testing links, require all three anchors, and record tested commit/input hashes. Spec L221: "30 s idle after the last download, clicking each link-out (intercepted, not followed)". No leak demonstrated.

C3 exempts whole parts containing removed-slide hyperlinks. Unrelated decoration damage in those parts escapes comparison. In-memory probe of pinned oracle deleted all content from such a layout and still returned no problems. Fix: normalize only authorized hyperlink elements and relationships, then compare remaining XML. Spec L151: "Every other part is kept: binary parts byte for byte, XML parts equal after canonicalisation". This proves test weakness, not actual logo deletion by fill.

G0's placeholder-only result is hardcoded true and excluded from script_clean. Shared reader ignores non-placeholder text shapes (f6c30a9:tests/oracle.py:127-134), so extra text outside placeholders can evade claimed check. Fix: inspect every text-bearing output shape and include result in gate. Spec L212: "every text in a placeholder".

Validator runner silently omits missing required outputs. G0 decks are discovered by glob; C10 downloads are included only when present. Both are gitignored, so validation can report success without either family. Fix: require explicit artifact manifest, fail incomplete runs, and cover all output families claimed by C5. Spec L217: "reports zero errors on every output". This finding concerns runner behavior, not excluded SDK installation.

C15 checker can succeed with missing cases or changed numbers. It skips absent outputs, accepts numeric substrings such as 14 inside 114, and exits successfully after printing FAIL. Fix: require three named cases, compare numeric tokens, and exit nonzero on failure. Spec L227: "on three notes" and "keeps every number from the notes". Current saved report contains three passing cases; no current numeric loss established.

Evidence limits: G0 visual judgments reference untracked renders (f6c30a9:qa/g0/G0-RESULT.md:39-47). C10 reports two equal outputs, but browser artifacts are untracked and report lacks hashes (f6c30a9:qa/e2e/c9-report.json:145-158; f6c30a9:qa/e2e/c10-report.json:1-14). These measurements cannot be independently reconstructed from pinned artifacts. C12's recorded warm result is 4.985 seconds, within its bar, not a rounded failure (f6c30a9:qa/e2e/c12-report.json:47-50).

## elderly.gov.hk: why level 1 is small and level 2 is large
This is the template's own styling, not a wrong paragraph level from the fill. Each part is one XML line, so the citations name the element path.

- The fill writes the right levels. `ppt/slides/slide2.xml` of the filled deck: level-1 lines are `<a:p>` with no `a:pPr`, so `lvl` is 0; level-2 lines carry `<a:pPr lvl="1"/>` (本地送貨準時率…, then 試行 AI 排程 under `lvl="1"`).

- The layout restyles level 1 only. `ppt/slideLayouts/slideLayout20.xml` (`1_Title and Content`), the `p:sp` holding `<p:ph idx="10"/>`: `a:lstStyle/a:lvl1pPr marL="0" indent="0"` with `<a:buNone/>` and `<a:defRPr sz="1867">` in grey (`tx1`, lumMod 75000, lumOff 25000). It has no `lvl2pPr`.

- Level 2 falls through to the master. `ppt/slideMasters/slideMaster3.xml`, `p:txStyles/p:bodyStyle/a:lvl2pPr`: `<a:buChar char="•"/>` and `<a:defRPr sz="2400">` in `tx1` black. So level 2 is bulleted, black and 24 pt under an 18.67 pt level 1.

python-pptx re-sorts relationships by Id and makes absolute targets relative when it saves. Real templates keep them in another order (EDB, elderly.gov.hk, Microsoft and USC all did), so C3 flagged 3 to 16 changed `.rels` parts per template. `fill` now puts the template's own bytes back for every kept part whose meaning is unchanged. A new fixture, `rels-order`, covers it, and an isolated mutation shows the test failing without the fix (`qa/failure-demos/c3-rels-order-*.txt`).

Second fix, from Fable's QA of the renders: a copied slide-number field kept its source slide's cached text, so Quick Look showed 2 on every Microsoft slide and 7 on slide 4. `fill` now writes each slide's own number into the cached text of every `slidenum` field it places. PowerPoint recomputes the field on open either way. C4 checks it on `footer-active`; the mutation demo is `qa/failure-demos/c4-slidenum-text-*.txt`.
